Rushing yards, attempts, touchdowns and longest rush

notes: Only NFL player props are collected and published.
Preseason box scores are excluded from every projection and betting decision.
Current ESPN rosters remove players who are no longer on the upcoming team and supply position and injury context.
A transient incomplete roster pull is retried once; any team still unverified remains WATCH-only rather than being allowed to qualify.
Prior-season form is automatically reduced until four current-season games are available.
Opponent adjustments compare position-level production allowed with the league median, then shrink and cap the result at 12%.
The 10,000-run matchup simulator refreshes from the same ESPN form and defense data as the betting model.
Daily Parlays mix 3–4 fresh same-book prop legs, retain the sample and confidence safeguards, require market variety, and apply an extra same-game correlation haircut.
Touchdowns, field goals, interceptions and sacks use count-stat probability handling and stricter reliability gates.
Sportsbook consensus is never treated as an independent model by itself.
Each exact prop publishes the best observed price from the configured Ontario-regulated brand allowlist.
Covers supplies public comparison-page market lines. The observation time is recorded; it is not represented as a sportsbook-originated update time.
An exact one-sided offer can qualify only as a LEAN after an extra edge reserve; no opposite price or no-vig probability is invented.
Key-based odds requests are disabled. If the public page is unavailable or changes shape, existing wagers and keyless player projections are preserved.
A wager enters My Ledger only after the user reviews the live price and clicks Add.
No odds API credentials are read or sent by the scheduled build.

meta.prior_note: 55% ESPN FPI / 45% win totals + prior results; base was 55% market win totals / 45% last season, plus market-spread prior fading from 35% as results arrive

settings._comment: Every knob the model uses. Edit this file, commit, and the next scheduled run recalculates everything. This is the web version of the workbook's Control Panel sheet.

bankroll._size_off_note: 'settled' sizes off the bankroll implied by settled bets only, so a stake never depends on the outcome of the bet it is sizing. 'starting' always sizes off the starting bankroll, like the workbook did.

tiers._note: Tier input is compressed expected return per unit at the offered price, capped by no-vig model value, minus selection and confidence reserves. Probability edge is published separately. Version 2026-09-06-ev2; historical tiers stay frozen.
tiers._nfl_note: Far lower than the college thresholds, because the NFL market is the sharpest in North American sport: 32 teams, enormous handle, every book pricing the same 16 games all week. Real NFL edges live between 1% and 4%. A model reporting a 12% edge on a Sunday side has found a bug, not an opportunity.

lock_rules._note: Extra conditions a play must ALSO satisfy to be called BEST BET. The label is reserved for the rare spot where the model, the market and the data all point the same way -- everything else tops out at GOOD no matter how big the raw number looks.
lock_rules._min_line_gap_note: Points of disagreement between the model's line and the market's. A big probability edge on a line the model actually agrees with is a pricing artefact, not a read.
lock_rules._max_line_gap_note: The other side of the same coin. If the model is seven points away from a market that prices this game for a living, the model is the one that is wrong.
lock_rules._adverse_move_note: Points the market may move AGAINST our side since we first saw the line before BEST BET is withdrawn. The market moving away from you after you form an opinion is the clearest signal available that the opinion is the stale one.

tiers._best_reachability_note: 4% clears the 5.5% compression ceiling minus the 1% selection reserve at mature confidence. The previous 4.5% threshold equalled the unattainable asymptote. Existing BEST data/price/movement locks also apply.

model._projection_blend_note: How much of the model's DISAGREEMENT with the market line survives into the number it actually bets. 0.55 keeps just over half. The market spread is the single best public estimate of a game, so the model's job is to nudge it, not to replace it. This is where the humility belongs -- it is legible ('our line vs their line') in a way that blending raw probabilities never is.
model._max_disagreement_note: Soft ceiling, in points, on how far the model's line may sit from the market's. Applied with a tanh squeeze rather than a hard clip, so a 3-point disagreement passes through nearly untouched while a 15-point one -- which is always a data problem, not an insight -- compresses to about 6.
model._edge_compression_note: The fix for absurd edges. Raw edge is squeezed through max_edge * tanh(raw / max_edge), so 2% stays 1.9%, 4% becomes 3.5%, and a nonsense 20% lands at 5.4% instead of screaming BEST BET. Small edges pass through nearly unchanged; large ones asymptote. Every number shown on the site is the compressed one, and the raw figure is kept alongside it so you can see what was squeezed.
model._market_blend_note: A second, smaller dose of humility applied at the probability level, on top of the projection blend above. Kept low precisely because projection_blend already anchors the line to the market -- blending twice at full strength would leave the model with no opinion at all.
model._margin_sd_note: Standard deviation of NFL final margins. The workbook used 13.5; the modern-era number is closer to 13.2 and it barely matters, but it is measurable so it should be measured.
model._ties_note: NFL regular-season games can end tied (~0.2% of games) and a moneyline tie is graded as a PUSH, not a loss. The workbook priced ties as impossible and the college model splits them; here they are priced and graded as pushes.
model._hfa_note: Modern NFL home-field advantage, in points. It has fallen a long way from the old 3-point rule of thumb; 2015-2024 sits near 1.7-2.2. The pipeline solves it from results and shrinks toward this number early in the year.
model._rest_note: Points per day of rest advantage. Small in the NFL because almost every team is on the same weekly cycle -- it exists to price Thursday games, bye weeks and the London turnaround, not to reward a normal Sunday.
model._timezone_note: Points deducted from a west-coast team playing a 1pm Eastern kickoff, the one travel effect with real evidence behind it.
model._divisional_note: Division games are played twice a year by teams that know each other cold, and they run measurably tighter and lower-scoring than the same matchup between strangers. Small, and applied only to the total.
model._per_team_hfa_note: Solve each stadium's own home-field value and shrink it hard toward the league number. Denver's altitude and Seattle's noise are real; most of the other 30 are noise, and the shrinkage is what tells them apart.

calibration._min_samples_note: Graded calls required before the model is allowed to correct its own probabilities. High on purpose -- a recalibration fitted on forty results is fitted to noise, and is worse than no correction at all.
calibration._clamp_note: Safety rails on the Platt fit. A wild fit means something upstream is broken; the correct response is a nudge and a warning in the log, not letting one strange month invert the model.

model._early_season_shrink_note: How hard a team's current-season rating is pulled back toward its preseason prior before it has min_games_for_full_confidence games played.
model._selection_haircut_note: Winner's-curse conservatism, subtracted from every estimated edge before tiering. You only bet where the model disagrees with the market, which is exactly where the model's own error is largest, so selected edges are overstated even when the model is calibrated across all games. Raise it to bet less and more selectively; re-measure it with `python -m pipeline.backtest` rather than trusting this number.
model._confidence_penalty_note: Bounded expected-return reserve: (1-confidence) × 1.8%, plus the selection haircut. Confidence never multiplies the tier thresholds.

ratings._mov_cap_note: NFL blowouts are rarer and less informative than college ones; capping margin at 24 keeps a 45-7 Thursday nighter from dominating the fit.
ratings._recency_note: Half-life in team-games (x7 = days). 8 means a game from two months ago counts about half as much as this week's. Shorter than the college half-life because NFL rosters and form move faster.
ratings._prior_regression_note: Fraction of last season's solved rating retained as this season's preseason prior. ~0.55 matches the observed year-over-year correlation of NFL team strength.
ratings._fpi_weight_note: Share of the independent preseason prior taken from current-season ESPN NFL FPI. FPI adds predictive EPA, QB/player and unit information; the remaining 45% keeps market win totals plus this model's prior results as a separate opinion.
ratings._market_spread_prior_weight_note: Maximum preseason weight on ratings solved from current point spreads. It fades to zero as results arrive and stays below 50% so the model cannot erase every edge by copying the same market it evaluates.
ratings._market_spread_ratings_note: Solve a power rating per team from the posted point spreads and use it as the early-season prior, fading it out as each team plays. In Week 2 the market's opinion -- which has already priced the draft, free agency and the quarterback's ankle, with real money behind it -- is worth more than the model's own one-game sample.
ratings._win_totals_note: Blend the preseason prior with the market's own 2026 win totals from config/win_totals.json. The market's preseason opinion is better than last season's results alone, which is exactly why the workbook seeded ratings from win totals in the first place.

injuries._note: Auto-adjustment from ESPN's injury feed, QB-weighted. Every point applied is shown on the game card and written into the JSON, so nothing moves invisibly.
injuries._position_points_note: Points of team strength lost when that player is fully OUT. The starting-QB number is the only large one and it is deliberately conservative: market studies put a starting QB's value between 3 and 7 points depending on the backup, and this model has no way to know how good the backup is.
injuries._max_team_points_note: Hard cap on how much one team's injury list can move the line. Without it, a long Week 14 report stacks a dozen small deductions into a fake double-digit swing.
injuries._total_note: How much a team's offensive injury load pulls the projected combined score down.

weather._provider_note: Open-Meteo is keyless, free, and does not rate-limit a job that asks for 16 forecasts twice a day. No account, no secret, nothing to expire.
weather._wind_note: [mph, points off the projected total]. Wind is the only weather variable with a large, repeatable effect on NFL scoring -- it kills the deep passing game and the kicking game together. Rain and cold matter far less than television makes you believe.

filters._note: Bets that fail these are still shown with the reason. No model pick is auto-logged: My Ledger contains only wagers the user explicitly adds in the browser.
filters._max_bets_per_game_note: Correlation guard. A team's moneyline and its spread are close to the same bet, so taking both is one position at double the variance Kelly assumed.
filters._max_plays_per_week_note: Hard cap on how many bets one NFL week can produce, best edges first. A 16-game slate with a 2.5% threshold will happily qualify twenty plays; that is a spray, not a staking plan.
filters._bet_within_days_note: Games further out than this are priced and displayed but not staked. Seeing an edge three weeks early is useful; betting into a market that thin is not, and the number will move several times before kickoff. The card shows the date the play opens.
filters._bet_preseason_note: Preseason games are priced and displayed but never tiered as a play. Starter snap counts, not team strength, decide preseason games, and no rating model sees the coach's snap plan.

data._sweep_note: Re-fetch the whole remaining season every run, not just the next few weeks. Books post lines for all 18 regular-season weeks in August, so this is real data sitting there unused -- and sweeping it every run is what captures the opening number and every move since, for the whole season rather than the fortnight in front of us. Costs about nine HTTP requests.
data._outlook_note: Project every future game that has a posted line, however far out, and publish it as a look-ahead view. These are NOT tracked in the shadow book and NOT staked: a call frozen four months early would be graded against a line that moved twenty times, which would corrupt the accuracy record rather than extend it.
data._lookahead_note: How far ahead games are priced. Set wide on purpose: books post Week 1 lines in August, and a 14-day window in late August sees nothing but preseason -- an empty board that looks broken and is not. Pricing early also captures the opening number, which is where closing line value comes from.

settings._comment: Every knob in the model. Edit this file, commit, and the next run recalculates everything. This is the web version of the workbook's Settings sheet.

tiers._note: Tier input is compressed expected return per unit at the offered price, capped by no-vig model value, minus selection and confidence reserves. Probability edge is published separately. Version 2026-09-06-ev2; historical tiers stay frozen.

model._projection_blend_note: Fraction of the model's disagreement with the posted line that survives into the actionable projection. College markets are softer than the NFL, so half survives, but the market remains the scale anchor.
model._max_spread_disagreement_note: Raw spread disagreements are squeezed through a tanh curve before projection_blend is applied. This stops an early-season rating-scale miss from turning a 40-point favourite into a coin flip while preserving ordinary 2-6 point opinions.
model._edge_compression_note: Displayed/actionable probability edge is squeezed through 9.5% * tanh(raw/9.5%). Small edges remain useful; a bogus 20% edge is shown near the ceiling instead of presented as a real 20% advantage. Raw edge remains in the data for auditing.
model._market_blend_note: Weight given to the de-vigged market probability. Higher = more humble. The market is a consensus of everyone with money on the line; a single rating model should not assume it knows better.
model._early_season_shrink_note: How hard to pull a team's current-season rating back toward its preseason prior before it has min_games_for_full_confidence games played.
model._confidence_penalty_note: Bounded expected-return reserve: (1-confidence) × 1.8%, plus the selection haircut. Confidence never multiplies the tier thresholds.
model._selection_haircut_note: Winner's-curse conservatism, subtracted from every estimated edge before tiering. You only bet where the model disagrees with the market, which is also where the model's own error is largest, so selected edges are overstated even when the model is calibrated across all games -- walk-forward simulation puts that gap at 9-15 points of probability. Raise it to bet less and more selectively. Re-measure with `python -m pipeline.backtest` on your own data rather than trusting this number.
model._market_blend_calibration_note: 0.50 was chosen because it minimised out-of-sample calibration error in walk-forward simulation across both a sharp market and a soft one (mean absolute gap 0.045-0.050 at 0.50, vs 0.049-0.073 at 0.35 and 0.055-0.058 at 0.65). Profitability in simulation depends entirely on how inefficient you assume the market is, so it was not used to pick this value.
model._min_books_for_full_confidence_note: One complete sportsbook quote is a real offer, not a consensus. Until two distinct books are observed, confidence is capped and every surviving play is LEAN-only with reduced stake.

ratings._current_season_prior_strength_note: Bayesian weight retained on the preseason prior while current-season results accumulate. Roughly six team-games of evidence; strong enough to stabilize September, light enough for October results to take over.
ratings._prior_season_weight_note: How much last season's solved ratings carry into this season's preseason prior (regression to the mean).
ratings._prior_regression_note: Fraction of last season's rating retained as the preseason prior. 0.62 ~ typical year-over-year correlation in CFB.
ratings._fpi_weight_note: Share of the preseason margin prior taken from current-season ESPN FPI. The other 15% remains this model's regressed prior-season solve, so FPI keeps its correct point scale without simply replacing the independent model.
ratings._fpi_scoring_weight_note: Lower weight for FPI's offense/defense/special-teams components in the totals model. Unit splits are more uncertain than the headline FPI rating, so the internal scoring solve retains the majority weight.
ratings._recency_note: Half-life in team-games (x7 = days). 14 means a game from ~3 months ago counts half as much as this week's.

filters._note: Bets that fail these are shown but never auto-logged to the ledger.
filters._preferred_price_note: Prices outside this preferred band may still qualify, but are capped at LEAN and staked at half size.
filters._hard_price_note: Absolute pricing stop. Rows beyond this range stay visible as AVOID; they are never logged or staked.
filters._max_bets_per_game_note: Correlation guard. 1 means the model picks only its single best angle on a game (ML and ATS on the same team are ~the same bet).
filters._soft_guard_note: Crossing a soft rail caps the play at LEAN and reduces stake rather than deleting it from the actionable middle of the board.
filters._max_spread_projection_gap_note: Hard spread blind-spot stop. Moderate disagreements are handled by the soft rail first.
filters._guard_headroom_note: A safety rail must never sit below the bar it is protecting. Edge rises with the raw model/market gap, so a confidence-scaled tier threshold is itself a minimum raw gap in disguise; if the ceiling below lands under that minimum, the two guards overlap to zero and NOTHING can qualify at any price. That is exactly what silenced the entire 2026 opening slate. This widens the ceiling, only when it has to, to sit 35% above whatever a LEAN currently requires. Set to 1.0 to disable and apply the ceilings literally.
filters._max_raw_market_prob_gap_note: Hard rejection for truly extreme disagreements before market blending can hide a ratings failure.
filters._thin_data_guard_note: Before both teams have meaningful current-season data, moderate gaps are LEAN-only at reduced stake; only genuinely extreme gaps are rejected.
filters._max_plays_per_week_note: Hard cap on how many bets the model logs in a calendar week, best edges first. Without it a loose threshold plus a full Saturday slate will happily stake 60 bets.

odds_health.message: Only complete two-sided sportsbook prices are actionable.

quote_coverage.note: Only one sportsbook source is available; confidence and stake are reduced

fpi_audit.method: Same-time pregame forecasts. Current FPI plus season results versus fixed FPI plus games after its source date. This baseline was captured during the season; it is not a preseason snapshot.
